messages.subject: supported platforms;  ready for 1.0.4
parts:
OK, I think we're ready to go for 1.0.4, at least
on the Stan side. Jiqiang -- is RStan ready to go out?

Daniel and I updated:

https://code.google.com/p/stan/wiki/TestUnitStatus?ts=1355524270&updated=TestUnitStatus

to reflect the various compilers, defaults, flags and our
support desiderata (which boils down to making sure default
versions of everything work for R).

If nobody objects, we'll roll out Stan 1.0.4 on Monday.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: supported platforms;  ready for 1.0.4
parts:
On Friday, December 14, 2012 5:35:51 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
OK, I think we're ready to go for 1.0.4, at least
on the Stan side.  Jiqiang -- is RStan ready to go out?

Daniel and I updated:

https://code.google.com/p/stan/wiki/TestUnitStatus?ts=1355524270&updated=TestUnitStatus

to reflect the various compilers, defaults, flags and our
support desiderata (which boils down to making sure default
versions of everything work for R).

If nobody objects, we'll roll out Stan 1.0.4 on Monday.

Not objecting to the release, but you keep putting inaccurate things in the wiki. For example, according to

http://clang.llvm.org/docs/UsersManual.html#id30

clang (like g++) defaults to gnu99 if left unspecified, which our makefile currently does. I wouldn't be opposed to having the makefile specify -std=c++98 or -std=c++03, which I think would be preferable to possibly relying on g++ extensions in subtle ways.

Also, somewhat tangentially related and largely unrelated to the release of 1.0.4, but I would question our advice (and default) to use O=3 as opposed to O=2. I haven't yet seen any empirical evidence that O=3 makes Stan noticeably faster, but it does use more RAM and goes against the compiler's defaults.

Ben

However, I've only done that for various configurations on my laptop, so I don't know about other OSes.

to reflect the various compilers, defaults, flags and our

versions of everything work for R).

Thanks for finding that reference. We looked at it too. gnu99 refers to the C language and not C++. If you look at the C++ language options, clang doesn't even enumerate the valid options. The closest I got to a list was in their doxygen doc, but that didn't specify a default mode. 

I think I read somewhere that they use the gcc / g++ defaults unless otherwise specified, but I can't find the link right now.

I also suspect that the wiki is wrong to say that -std=c++03 is used by default on Windows. I assume it would be the same as g++-4.6. But if for whatever reason some compiler is defaulting to something other than -std=gnu98, then Stan by default would be compiled with gnu extensions sometimes and without gnu extensions other times. In which case, I don't see why we shouldn't override that by specifying either -std=c++98 or -std=c++03 in makefile.

Ben
